subject: Mosaic AI — capacity orchestration and regional sizing for onboarding
messages:
From: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@skyline.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Park <oliver.park@mosaic.ai>
Date: 2027-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Mosaic proof-of-concept -> expected steady and burst needs

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. To help our procurement and infra teams we need a concrete recommended footprint for the POC + month-1 ramp so we can line up budgets and cloud approvals. High level: our POC will target 50k daily queries, mostly short chat/assistant calls (mean context 512 tokens), and we expect a production cutover in ~6–8 weeks if POC performance aligns.

Can you share your recommended dedicated pool sizing by region (US/EU/APAC) — both sustained baseline and an initial burst buffer for the first 4 weeks? Also we need an estimate of the lead time to guarantee this capacity as a reserved tranche (SLA window, commit notice).

Attachments: example request template (we'll attach internal compliance checklist separately).

Best,
Maya
Sr. Platform Ops, Mosaic AI

---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@mosaic.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-15T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic proof-of-concept -> expected steady and burst needs

Maya — thanks, outline below (summary first, full assumptions attached):

Summary recommendation (sustained / burst buffer):
- US: 60 A100-class sustained slots, 30-slot burst (30/50% buffer)
- EU: 40 A100-class sustained slots, 20-slot burst
- APAC (SG): 18 A100-class sustained slots, 10-slot burst

Notes: we express in A100-class equivalents to keep spec stable across regions — if you want H100 or newer hardware we can convert with a delta multiplier. Baseline sizing assumes: 50k daily queries, average request 512 tokens input + 128 tokens expected output, concurrency profile peak 120 QPS global with US-heavy traffic (55%).

Lead time & commitment options:
- 2-week notice for reserved tranche allocation where spare capacity exists; 6–8 weeks for guaranteed procurement-backed capacity during heavy holiday windows.
- If Mosaic can commit to a 6-month reserved tranche we can prioritize pool placement and offer a stepped discount and firm SLA.

I've attached a detailed workbook with token-level cost, expected latency SLOs, and canary plan (start US-only POC, then EU day+7, APAC day+14).

Next steps: If the numbers look reasonable, can Karthik and Ben join a short call later today to lock timelines and sign the tranche letter of intent?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mosaic_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf; mosaic_surge_model_sheet.xlsx

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@mosaic.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-16T08:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic proof-of-concept -> expected steady and burst needs

Maya, Naomi — quick operational clarifications and one alternative sizing option.

Operational clarifications:
- "Slots" above map to 1x A100-80GB equivalent GPU with our serving runtime. We can provide quantized NPU variants (H100-equivalent runtime) but those will change request concurrency and per-token cost.
- Burst buffer strategy: we recommend a short-lived burst pool with automatic routing fallback to regional lower-cost variants if sustained burst persists beyond 72 hours.
- Canary windows: we propose 72-hour canary in US (full traffic split 80/20 for production vs fallback) to validate KV caching effectiveness.

Alternative lower-commit option (if Mosaic prefers smaller initial financial commitment):
- US: 40 sustained + 20 burst (convertible to 60/30 within 30 days)
- EU: 24 sustained + 12 burst
- APAC: 12 sustained + 6 burst

This alternative reduces upfront reserved commitment while preserving a prioritized path to scale. If Mosaic signals a hard commit we will lock the larger footprint and start procurement immediately.

I'll schedule a 30-minute slot; Naomi please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

---

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@mosaic.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@mosaic.ai>, procurement@mosaic.ai
Date: 2027-11-17T10:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic proof-of-concept -> expected steady and burst needs

Hi Naomi / Karthik — appreciate the fast turnaround. The alternative lower-commit option looks closer to our procurement comfort zone. A few clarifying questions from finance and infra:

1) Can you provide a per-hour and per-month cost delta between the two options (we need a quick TCO for leadership) — include token-level cost assumptions.
2) What happens operationally if we hit sustained burst in APAC beyond 7 days? Will requests be routed to EU or fallback to hosted instances and what are the latency expectations?
3) On the contractual side we need the minimum lead time guaranteed for converting from the alternative to the larger footprint (Karthik mentioned 30 days) — we need that in writing to present to our CFO.

Proposed next steps: we can sign a 3-month tranche for the alternative footprint with a 30-day conversion clause to the larger tranche. Can you please send an updated SOW/LoI reflecting those terms and the cost delta?

Thanks,
Oliver Park
VP Engineering, Mosaic AI

---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@mosaic.ai>, Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@mosaic.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-18T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic proof-of-concept -> expected steady and burst needs

Oliver — thanks, happy to move forward on the 3-month alternative tranche with a 30-day conversion clause. Actions I'm taking and deliverables: 

1) SOW/LoI: Ben will draft and share a short LoI today that includes conversion clause (30 days notice to convert from alternative to full footprint) and the 72-hour sustained-burst failover flows.
2) Cost delta: Ben will attach a per-hour and pro-rated monthly cost table (A100-equivalent) with token-level assumptions and expected unit economics.
3) Operational doc: Karthik will provide a 1-page runbook describing APAC > EU routing, expected median added latency (APAC->EU fallback: +80–120ms median), and the automatic fallback thresholds (72 hrs sustained > 60% burst usage triggers scale and routing).
4) Timeline: upon signed LoI we will prioritize pool placement. Given current procurement windows, guaranteed allocation for the alternative tranche is 10 business days; conversion to full footprint (subject to hardware procurement) is guaranteed within 30 calendar days from conversion notice except during major holiday procurement freezes (Nov 21–Dec 10 will add an extra 10 business days).

I'll send a consolidated package (LoI + cost table + runbook) by EOD PST. If the Mosaic team can sign by Friday we can start the US canary as early as Nov 29.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments to follow: mosaic_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf (updated), mosaic_surge_model_sheet.xlsx (updated)
